item.title: Indonesia Vows to Protect Investment at Launch of Battery, Solar, Aluminum Plants
item.description: Indonesia is committed to respecting and safeguarding all investments, President Prabowo Subianto said on Thursday, as he launched nickel- and aluminum-based projects worth billions. Prabowo spoke at a launch ceremony for the commercial operations of industrial facilities and the construction of other projects in an …
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded:
Indonesia is committed to respecting and safeguarding all investments, President Prabowo Subianto said on Thursday, as he launched nickel- and aluminum-based projects worth billions.

Prabowo spoke at a launch ceremony for the commercial operations of industrial facilities and the construction of other projects in an industrial park at Weda Bay, partly controlled by Chinese steelmaker Tsingshan Holding Group.

He also launched the first exports of EV batteries, produced by REPT Battero, at the ceremony.

“I emphasize here an Indonesian government commitment to respect and safeguard all investments, from wherever,” he said. “We are committed to safeguarding our partnership as well as possible. It is a matter of honor for the Indonesian people to support our partners.”

A drone view shows nickel processing facilities at the Indonesia Weda Bay Industrial Park in Central Halmahera Regency, North Maluku province, Indonesia, in this handout picture released October 8, 2026. Indonesia Presidential Palace/Handout via REUTERS

Indonesia has attracted massive investment into its metal industry and smelting, mainly from China, with firms drawn to its rich nickel reserves, but recent policies have raised concerns from some business players.

Chinese companies operating in Indonesia have called for more business-friendly policies, warning in a letter to the president that tighter mining quotas, higher taxes and a new pricing formula are driving up costs and threatening investment.

Country Is World’s Top Exporter of Nickel Products

Indonesia, which holds the world’s largest nickel ore reserves, banned raw nickel exports in 2020 to promote domestic processing industries.

The policy has helped Indonesia become the world’s top exporter of nickel products, accounting for around 60% of global supply, with export value rising from $3.3 billion in 2017 to over $33 billion by 2024.

The Investment Ministry said companies investing in the new projects at Weda Bay include PT Guang Ching Nickel Cobalt, PT Weda Bay Aluminum, and PT Flatsolar Energy Indonesia.

A drone view shows nickel processing facilities at the Indonesia Weda Bay Industrial Park in Central Halmahera Regency, North Maluku province, Indonesia, in this handout picture released October 8, 2026. Indonesia Presidential Palace/Handout via REUTERS

The four projects were worth $3.4 billion, while investment in six other projects is expected to reach $6.8 billion, investment minister Rosan Roeslani said at the same event on Thursday.

The new constructions include facilities to produce nickel-based battery material, battery components, and photovoltaic glass for solar panels, Rosan said. He added that the development of two aluminum plants also launched on Thursday.
